newsitem.title: CANADA: Quebec estimates 1997/98 spending at C$39.8 bln.
newsitem.headline: Quebec estimates 1997/98 spending at C$39.8 bln.

text.p: Quebec Treasury Board President Jacques Leonard said on Tuesday that the government estimated its 1997/98 spending at C$39.8 billion, a decline of C$851 million or 2.1 percent from fiscal 1996/97.

The estimate included C$33.9 billion of program spending and C$5.9 billion in debt service costs for fiscal 1997/98 ending March 31, 1998. The spending estimates compared with probable total spending of C$40.6 billion for 1996/97.
Probable program spending in 1996/97, which ends March 31, was estimated at C$34.7 billion, while debt service was estimated at C$5.9 billion.
Quebec's direct debt was C$76 billion, Leonard said.

Leonard unveiled the estimates in Quebec's National Assembly. Quebec is the only major Canadian province to release its spending estimates ahead of the full budget. The spending estimates do not include revenue or deficit figures.
Leonard said cleaning up Quebec's public finances would help the separatist Parti Quebecois government's drive toward independence for the French-speaking Canadian province.
"Healthy finances will give Quebeckers confidence. It is not negative for sovereignty," Leonard said.
Quebec said previously that it planned to balance its budget by fiscal 1999/2000 and had set deficit targets of C$3.275 billion for 1996/97, C$2.2 billion for 1997/98 and C$1.2 billion for 1998/99.
The latest spending estimates included C$2.33 billion of cuts in government costs for 1997/98. In 1996/97, Quebec instituted cost-cutting measures of C$2.25 billion.
The program spending cuts for 1997/98 included C$760 million in health and social services, C$683 million in education and C$189 million of savings in the welfare budget.
Leonard told a news conference that the separatist Parti Quebecois government would maintain spending objectives set out in its bid to balance the overall budget by 1999/2000.
"The Quebec government is on the right track. It is now well on its way to controlling expenses," Leonard told reporters in French.
"In the 1997/98 estimates, the government continues to focus on the objectives it has set out. The goal for 1998/99 and 1999/2000 will be to maintain a freeze on spending," Leonard said.
Meanwhile, talks continued on the proposed payroll cuts with unions representing Quebec's 440,000 public employees, including teachers, nurses and civil servants.
As part of its payroll cost reduction measures, the government is seeking to eliminate 15,000 public service sector jobs by July 1 through early retirement, attrition and severances.
